subject: Dedicated pool turnup: canary traffic plan & regional burst allocation
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Meyer <paul.meyer@aureliahealth.com>, platform@aureliahealth.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-06T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool turnup: canary traffic plan & regional burst allocation

Hi Paul / Aurelia platform team —

Thanks for the kickoff call today. Per our conversation, I wanted to share a concise plan for the dedicated GPU pool turnup and the canary/burst behavior we recommend for a low-risk go-live. Please review and confirm the three quick items below so engineering can provision and ops can schedule the netops window.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Primary region: us-west-2 (preferred), warm standby: us-east-1.
- Initial canary: 5% traffic for 6 hours -> 15% over 24h -> 30% steady by 72h (unless we see regressions).
- Autoscale policy: scale-up threshold at 70% GPU utilization sustained for 3m; scale delta +1 instance; burst capacity reserved for 30% above baseline for first 7 days.
- GPU spec: customer requested A100-80GB or equivalent (let us know if you prefer 80GB vs 40GB variants).

Actions needed from you:
1) Confirm target QPS during peak (you mentioned "~180 QPS" on the call; need written confirmation).
2) Provide any maximum sequence lengths in samples (tokens) for inference templates — affects KV cache sizing.
3) Approve the proposed canary ramp (5 -> 15 -> 30) or propose alternative cadence.

Attachments: Helix_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (MAL), capacity_requirements.csv (sample traffic profile).

Notes for internal ops (cc’d):
- Rishi / Karthik: please prioritize a single reserved pool in us-west-2 with a warm standby in us-east-1. We’d like to enable prefix caching and a short prefix TTL for canary sessions.
- Soojin: can you pre-stage the quantization profile (int8 fast-path) for the selected model family and confirm fallback model variant in case memory pressure is observed?

I’ll follow up with a short runbook for the canary (expected by EOD).

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

--
Attachments: Helix_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (Excel, 42KB), capacity_requirements.csv (CSV, 6KB)

From: Paul Meyer <paul.meyer@aureliahealth.com>

Cc: platform@aureliahealth.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-07T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool turnup: canary traffic plan & regional burst allocation

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick confirmations from Aurelia:
1) Peak target QPS is 200 (we were conservative on the call). Sustained business-hours baseline ~110 QPS.
2) Typical sequence length: median ~120 tokens; 95th percentile under 420 tokens. We’ll attach a sample traffic extract in follow-up.
3) Canary cadence looks fine; we’d prefer a slightly longer second step (5% -> 10% over 12h -> 25% over 48h -> 30% by 72h) because our UI load can spike on batch jobs.

One ask: can you include SOC2 evidence (report snapshot) and an estimated RPO/RTO for the dedicated pool? Our security team will want to see the SLA implications before signing the MPA.

We’re good with us-west-2 primary and us-east-1 warm standby. Confirm when you want us to open a maintenance window with our network team (ideally next Tue or Wed evening PST).

—Paul
Paul Meyer
Platform Lead, Aurelia Health
paul.meyer@aureliahealth.com

Team —

Thanks Monica and Paul for the confirmation. Quick internal alignment and next steps from my side:

Operational recommendations (we should align in this thread):
- Canary ramp: accept Paul's slightly extended ramp (5% -> 10% over 12h -> 25% over 48h -> 30% by 72h). Document in runbook.
- Autoscale policy: implement GPU-utilization threshold at 65% sustained for 180s to be conservative during canary; aggressive scale policy can be relaxed after 7-day observation window.
- Burst pool: reserve N+2 instances (calculated from Paul's baseline/peak numbers) and cap burst to 30% above committed baseline for first 14 days; billing footnote will be included in the MPA.
- Fallback: add automatic routing to a smaller model variant (quantized int8) if tail latency > 1.2s for >5% of requests in a 10m window.

Action items (owners):
- Karthik: open provisioning ticket with infra (include instance SKU preference: A100-80GB or H100 if available) and estimate lead time (ETA). Create ticket in JIRA and link.
- Soojin: prepare quantization profile and pre-warm cache keys; provide canary_runbook.md by EOD Monday.
- Monica: confirm maintenance window with Aurelia (Paul said Tue/Wed evening PST) and gather SOC2 snapshot for procurement.
- Kimberly: prepare billing footnote language for the MPA (30% burst for 14d with overage rules).

I’ve attached a short draft runbook (canary_runbook.md) and will follow up with a proposed JIRA ticket description. Deal id: HLX-482-DED.

Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

All —

Provisioning ticket created: REDW-7832 (attached pdf). ETA for pool delivery (us-west-2 primary): 6 business days if A100-80GB available; H100 option may add 2 days.

Operational checklist we will execute during the maintenance window:
- Pre-stage quant profile and warm KV caches for top 100 prefixes.
- Create ephemeral ingress routing for 5% canary and validate end-to-end traces.
- Monitor latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), GPU utilization, and token throughput; gate to escalate on p95 > 900ms for >10m.
- Enable autoscale as discussed (65% for 180s), with manual override to cap scale during canary if needed.
- Document and hand off billing footnote to Kimberly for MPA.

Please confirm the maintenance window slot (Paul suggested Tue/Wed evening PST). I’ll block 3 hours (start + 2h observation).

Karthik Iyer
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
